::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Jany 17th 1872  
**From:** Bray,  
**Manuscript:** MS Girton College,  Cambridge Yonge I 2
:::

My dear [William](people/person_669.qmd)
[I](people/person_78.qmd) have to thank you for some game which gives me an opportunity of writing to you.  I have thought much of your concern for [Lord Carnarvon](people/person_2277.qmd)’s illness, which must have been great;  I felt no little interest in it myself, as he is too good a man to be spared. I was the more alarmed from recollecting how few of his family have lived to be old :  now however I trust that he is doing well. What is your son [Arthur](people/person_653.qmd) doing?  I heard a report that he was abandoning the law, & taking to tuition work..

I have just been just been reading Miss Yonge’s ‘[Daisy Chain](cmy_books/cmybook_24.qmd)’, I am not sure whether for the 2d or the 3d time.  I wonder where it is ranked in her own estimation. I place it very high amongst her works, & consider it a model specimen of her peculiar powers. No one else could have written anything like it. The variety of the characters, the nice discrimination of their shades; the force with which they are drawn, the whole process of their development, strike me as admirable; & in spite of one or two <u>little</u> mistakes (such as making the boys catch crayfish in what must have been a tributary of the Severn, or the Wye, where they do not exist) & make me place it very high, not only amongst <u>her</u> works, but in the general region of fiction. Like [Walter Scott](people/person_1672.qmd)’s works & [my own Aunt](people/person_76.qmd)’s, I am never weary of reading it.

We have had a large family party for some weeks.  All our Sons have been more or less here except [Charles](people/person_77.qmd), whose residence will begin when Parliament meets:  but all are now breaking up. [^1]  [Mary](people/person_2278.qmd) is this morning crossing from Devon for another four month’s residence at Mentone.  She is not ill, but [Dr Quain](people/person_1219.qmd) urged it as a measure of precaution. 

With our affectionate regards to all your party I am very affly yours
J E Austen Leigh

---

[^1]: The Rev. James Edward Austen Leigh (1794-1874), nephew and biographer of Jane Austen, had been friends from childhood with Sir William Heathcote, whose mother was a friend of his aunt's.
[^2]: He had seven sons.
